items.mainDefect: When the join deadline expires, the loop breaks before terminating the current and remaining flusher workers, so they keep running after join returns.

secondary.defect: The join cleanup checks the process type in a way that does not recognize spawn-context (SpawnProcess) workers, so their termination is skipped.

items.mainDefect: Breaking out of worker cleanup when the join deadline expires means later workers never get a termination attempt.

secondary.defect: The cleanup's process type check does not recognize SpawnProcess workers.

items.mainDefect: Breaking out of the cleanup loop when the join deadline expires skips terminating the remaining workers, which stay alive after join and across partition reassignment.

secondary.defect: The termination pass uses the wrong process-type check, so spawn-context workers are not recognized.
